tasks.subject: Coins fall to the room floor and are dropped visibly onto the top deck
tasks.description:
Two changes, both confined to sim.js and render.js.

A. Remove the payout basin. render.js buildTray() currently builds a lit basin under the lower deck front edge: a floor slab at y -0.088 z 0.42 (0.22 deep), two side walls, a low front lip at z 0.532, a gold trim strip on that lip, and a warm PointLight at y 0.03 z 0.38. The user wants coins to fall to the floor and disappear instead of landing in a bucket. Delete the basin floor, the side walls, the front lip and its gold trim, and the basin light. KEEP the payout mouth on the cabinet front: the dark throat box, the two brass cheek blocks, and the gold lintel above the mouth. The player still needs to see where the payout window is in order to aim at it, so the mouth must stay readable as a slot in the cabinet face, not become a hole in nothing.

In sim.js: TRAY_Y (-0.081) becomes FLOOR_Y = -0.42, matching the room floor plane in render.js buildRoom(). TRAY_DWELL 1.9 becomes 0.9. Keep TRAY_FADE 0.5. MAX_TRAY 18 can stay. Export Sim.FLOOR_Y and keep Sim.TRAY_Y as an alias of the same value so the existing tools and render code do not break. In stepFall(), a paid coin must keep falling past the machine front all the way to FLOOR_Y, rest there, then fade. A lost coin behaves the same; it no longer needs to vanish at fy < -0.55 because the floor is now the destination.

In render.js fall-mesh sync: a coin should keep tumbling for the whole fall and only settle flat once it reaches FLOOR_Y. The existing settle test compares against TRAY_Y, so update it.

B. Make the drop visibly land on the TOP deck. Sim.drop() places the coin at TOP.dropZ (-0.36) on tier top with cy = TOP.y + 0.26 and fallT = 0.30, but the visual chute in render.js buildCabinet is hardcoded at chute.position.set(0, 0.30, -0.30). That mismatch makes the coin appear beside or behind the chute rather than released from it. Position the chute mouth exactly above the real drop point and drop height so the player watches the coin leave the chute and land on the top pile. Read G.Sim.TOP.dropZ and G.Sim.TOP.y at build time; do not hardcode -0.30.

Constraints: do not change deck geometry (top lip -0.15, top plate fwd -0.33, bottom payW 0.31, SCOOP 0.40) - those were tuned by tools/_topsweep.mjs and tools/_bal.mjs. Keep Sim.setDeck intact.

Acceptance: node --check passes on both files; node tools/selftest.mjs reports 13/13 PASS; node tools/_fall.mjs runs without error; a screenshot at desktop size shows no basin under the machine, and a screenshot taken shortly after a drop shows the coin in the air above the top deck.
tasks.output:
Payout basin deleted; coins now fall to the room floor and are dropped visibly from the chute onto the top deck.

A. Basin removed (render.js buildTray): deleted the basin floor slab, both side walls, the low front lip, its gold trim and the warm basin PointLight. Kept and reinforced the payout mouth on the cabinet face - dark throat, two brass cheeks, gold lintel - plus a dark back box (so the freed throat is not see-through) and a 30 mm shelf so the slot sits in a face. sim.js: TRAY_Y -0.081 -> FLOOR_Y -0.42 (same plane as render.js buildRoom's floor.position.y = -0.42), TRAY_DWELL 1.9 -> 0.9, TRAY_FADE 0.5 and MAX_TRAY 18 kept. stepFall now runs one floor path for paid and lost coins: they fall past the machine front, clamp at FLOOR_Y, rest for the dwell, then splice; the old "lost coin vanishes at fy < -0.55" branch is gone. Sim.FLOOR_Y exported, Sim.TRAY_Y kept as an alias of the same value so tools and render keep resolving. render.js fall sync: settle test, prop visibility and dwell default all keyed off FLOOR_Y; coins tumble the whole way and only flatten at the floor.

B. Drop now visibly leaves the chute onto the top deck. buildCabinet stops hardcoding chute.position.set(0, 0.30, -0.30) and reads G.Sim.TOP.dropZ / G.Sim.TOP.y at build time; live chute reported at (0, 0.48, -0.36), exactly Sim.drop()'s release point cy = TOP.y + 0.26, z = TOP.dropZ.

Also fixed two real game-feel bugs the screenshots exposed: render.js double-counted the drop arc (the coin was drawn up to 350 mm above the chute it had just left), and the sibling prop path divided by 0.30 while props spawn with fallT 0.38, which made the lift negative and floated prizes ~0.5 m above the chute at 0.24 scale. Both now trust the sim's cy; the prop scale reads drop progress off height above the deck so no cross-file constant matters. FIT_POINTS updated to the floor landing patch and the real chute mouth.

Deck geometry untouched: live constants read topLip -0.15, topFwd -0.33, topBack -0.48, topY 0.22, botPayW 0.31, botLip 0.30, botPlateFwd 0.02, SCOOP 0.40, GRAV 3.6, COIN_R 0.036, STEP 1/120; Sim.setDeck intact.

Screenshots: shots/feel/desktop-nobasin.png (bare floor tiled grid under the lower deck, no basin, two coins mid-fall down the front face), shots/feel/floor-rest.png (three coins resting flat on the room floor past the cabinet base), shots/feel/drop-in-air.png + zoom (coin hanging in the air directly under the chute mouth above the top pile). tasks.subject: Shake cooldown meter and a real collection detail page
tasks.description:
You own index.html and ui.js only. main.js and content.js belong to other members.

A. Shake cooldown, visible. Today the slap/shake ability is a hidden 3-charge budget in main.js (slapBudget = 3, +4200 ms recharge) with no on-screen indication at all. The player only learns it exists when it refuses. Replace the plain 拍機 button with a button that shows its own state: a charge count and a recharge progress. Implement two functions in ui.js for main.js to call:
  UI.slapState(state) where state is {left: number, max: number, ratio: number}, ratio 0..1 is the recharge progress toward the next charge.
  UI.slapFired() for the moment of use.
Render the meter as a thin progress bar along the bottom edge inside the button plus a small charge count, for example 2/3. When left is 0 the button shows a disabled look and the recharge bar fills; when a charge returns, pulse the button once so the player notices. Respect prefers-reduced-motion. The button must stay at least 44 px tall on phones.

B. Collection detail page. Today UI.openMuseum() renders a grid of small thumbnails with a name and nothing else; there is no way to learn about an item. Add a detail view inside the museum overlay: tapping or clicking a collected tile opens a full panel showing the 3D thumbnail at a large size, the name, the jyutping, the year, the owner, the personal memory text, the everyday use text, and the surprising fact. tasks.subject: Landed coins sink into the floor and lie at a 45° tilt
tasks.description:
CAPTAIN SPOT-CHECK of the t1 floor-landing work found a visible defect. Fix it in render.js (fall-mesh sync only). Do NOT touch sim.js physics constants, main.js or content.js — t4 and t6 are writing those right now.

EVIDENCE (reproduced, not a guess)
- Close-up screenshot: `shots/feel/_floorclose.png` and the crop `shots/feel/_zoom-floor.png`. A resting coin renders as a HALF-MOON / crescent: the disc is sliced by the floor plane, only a curved sliver of rim is visible above the tiles. It reads as a broken mesh, which is exactly what the user asked us to remove.
- Probe of the two resting coins: `[{"kind":"coin","fy":-0.42,"fax":-2.556,"faz":-4.4964,"r":0.036},{"kind":"coin","fy":-0.42,"fax":-7.006,"faz":1.6026,"r":0.036}]`.
- `render.js` fall sync (~line 1419-1445) does, every frame:
  `fm2.coin.rotation.set(fc.fax * 0.4, fc.faz * 0.2, fc.faz * 0.3);`
  then, only when resting:
  `if (fc.fy <= floorY + 0.002 && fc.kind === 'coin') { fm2.coin.rotation.x *= 0.75; fm2.coin.rotation.z *= 0.75; }`
  and positions it at `fc.fy + 0.007 + |jitter|`.

ROOT CAUSE (two separate faults, both must be fixed)
1. The "settle flat" damping is applied to a value that is REBUILT FROM SCRATCH every frame out of `fc.fax`. Multiplying by 0.75 therefore cannot converge: it just pins the coin at a fixed 75% of its tumble angle forever. With fax -2.556 the resting mesh sits at rotation.x = -0.767 rad (about -44°), i.e. standing on its edge.
2. The resting height is a constant `+0.007`, which is the half-thickness of a FLAT coin (coin cylinder is `CylinderGeometry(COIN_R, COIN_R, COIN_R * 0.42, 16)`, so half-thickness = COIN_R * 0.21 ≈ 0.00756). A coin tilted 44° needs up to COIN_R (0.036) of clearance, so it drives ~29 mm underground.

REQUIRED FIX
- When a coin is resting on the floor (fy at FLOOR_Y), stop re-deriving its rotation from `fax`. Give it a genuinely flat resting pose: face horizontal, spin only about its own vertical axis, e.g. `rotation.set(0, fc.faz * 0.35, 0)`. A coin's cylinder axis is +Y, so all-zero x/z IS flat.
- Set its height from the flat pose, not a magic 0.007: `floorY + COIN_R * 0.21 + jitter` (use the exported `G.Sim.COIN_R`, do not hardcode 0.036), so the visible face sits on the tiles with no z-fighting.
- Do the same class of fix for the prop branch: resting props are positioned `fc.fy + 0.006` while still carrying `fc.fax * 0.35` / `fc.faz * 0.2` / `fc.faz * 0.3` tilt, so a dropped prize also clips the floor. Give a resting prop an upright pose and a small lift.
- Keep the airborne tumble exactly as it is — the fall should still look like a tumbling coin; only the resting pose changes.

WHILE YOU ARE THERE (same file, small)
- The desktop frame now shows a large empty floor band in the lower third (you flagged this yourself). Tighten FIT_POINTS so the landing patch still fits but carries less dead floor, and re-run viewprobe on all five viewports.

1. A close-up of a resting coin (`shots/feel/_zoom-floor.png` regenerated) shows a FULL ROUND COIN face, not a crescent, and no part of it below the tiles.
2. A probe of resting coins reports a flat pose (rotation.x and rotation.z at 0) and fy > FLOOR_Y + COIN_R * 0.21.
3. Resting props are upright and not clipped by the floor.
4. `node --check render.js` exits 0.
5. `node tools/selftest.mjs` -> 13/13 PASS.
6. `node tools/viewprobe.mjs` -> all five viewports OK, and report the new dist/worstX/worstY per viewport.
Report the exact before/after probe values for the resting coin.
